questions.question: What is the primary reason for the conciseness of ancient Indian texts in an oral tradition?
options: It prevents conflicts between different fields of study
It makes the texts less complex for learners
It improves the efficacy of retention and transmission
It makes the texts deliberately difficult to keep it away from non-scholars

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three prasthāna-s that new schools of thought needed to pass?
options: Brahmasūtra
Daśopaniṣad
Bhagavad Gītā
Mahābhārata

questions.question: According to Ādi Śaṅkara's commentary on Gītā, what are the two 'Blocks of Dharma propounded in the Veda-s'?
options: Rituals & Meditation
Health & Wealth
Industriousness & Contemplation
Truth & Non-Violence

questions.question: According to Svāmī Vivekānanda, a person of true character will have the heart of a lion, from which he/she will derive what?
options: Infinite patience
Infinite strength
Infinite knowledge
Infinite memory

questions.question: What is the theme of the first six chapters of the Gītā?
options: The relationship between Jīva, Jagat, and Īśvara
The subtle aspects of perfection and modifying behavioural practices
The law of conservation of divinity
Karma Yoga, focusing on the individual in the context of work

questions.question: The author suggests that a dharmic way of life and belief in transcendence are conducive to what?
options: Developing character
Earning puṇya which facilitates happiness in future births
Leading a simple life with absolutely no material desires
Accepting the fast-paced changes of the current world

questions.question: What does the Sanskrit phrase 'निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन्' (nimittamātraṃ bhava savyasācin) from Chapter 11 of the Gītā mean?
options: You are my disciple and I will lead you on the right path
I am the path, the way, and the truth
Perform your duty without attachment to the results
Be, but an instrument, a medium that receives on behalf of a larger audience

questions.question: According to the text, what is the fundamental difference between Pain and Suffering?
options: Pain is emotional and only affects the mind, while suffering is purely physical
Pain is a natural process that the body experiences and eventually subsides, while suffering is a choice one makes when undergoing pain
Pain is long-lasting and unavoidable, while suffering can be instantly removed by magic or Yoga
Pain requires physical instruments to cause, whereas suffering is caused by emotional setbacks alone

questions.question: What does the text suggest is a major source of trouble or problems in the entire world, according to the profound message of the Gītā's very first śloka?
options: Wars, which lead to huge suffering and loss of lives
Greed for wealth, which creates a rift even among members of the same family
Attachment to "My People," worldly entities, positions, fame, and resources
Lack of knowledge of Dharma among leaders which causes them to take bad decisions

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'Dharma'?
options: It refers to the cardinal principle of sustainability
It means to conquer the entire world by peaceful means
It is a set of universal values that always hold true for every individual and every situation
It is a set of rituals which help establish world peace

questions.question: What is the first thing that happens when someone faces a crisis?
options: They do things that they repent later
They become very defensive
They are overcome by emotions and fears
They lose the power of discrimination

questions.question: What is the result of using intellect to defend the status quo in a crisis, rather than using it for objective decision-making?
options: It helps maintain a sense of calm
It results in making bad decisions
It strengthens one's conviction
It prevents the resolution of the crisis

questions.question: In the analogy of 'Pain vs Suffering,' what freedom do humans have?
options: The freedom to avoid all pain completely
The freedom to choose whether or not to suffer in response to pain
The freedom to change or shorten the course of pain, say, by dressing a wound with bandages
The freedom to overcome pain by using mantra-s and other supernatural techniques

questions.question: Why are valuable lessons not taught unless someone asks for them?
options: Because such knowledge is secret and is to be shared only with an elite set of people
Because they are difficult to explain and take lot of time and effort
Because they don't carry value unless someone is in need and also mentally prepared.
Because it requires the seeker to first declare their inferiority to the person they are seeking these lessons from

questions.question: What is necessary to achieve great things according to the teaching of Bhagavad Gītā?
options: Work quickly without procrastinating, as actions bring results
Focus only on the final goal without getting distracted by details of process
Brainstorm extensively and seek advice from experienced elders before embarking on any work
Retain a calm state and execute actions carefully at the ground level

questions.question: What is more effective when facing a deep problem?
options: Brainstorming ideas quickly to arrive at the solution intuitively
Seeking advice from as many people as possible and putting the ideas to vote
Brain stilling - Have a calm and settled mind and then contemplate
Allowing the problem to resolve itself rather than jumping in to solve it

questions.question: What should be the central objective of work?
options: To earn as much money as possible and retire early, to have time for spiritual pursuits
To compete with others and outperform them, as competitiveness leads to excellence
To complete all tasks to the highest possible state of perfection, so that success is guaranteed
To evolve ourselves, and make us complete and stronger individuals.

questions.question: How should one approach work?
options: Work without any result orientation
Let the motive be that the inner self gets stronger
Understand that we can never disengage from doing work
All of the above

questions.question: In the powerful imagery created by Yama for Naciketas, what is the chariot?
options: Body
Mind
Intellect
Ātman

questions.question: What kind of a leader is most likely to succeed in his leadership pursuits, as demonstrated by Kṛṣṇa?
options: One who treats all his followers equally & fairly
One who leads from the front by being willing to take up any task for the team
One who gives constructive feedback and pushes his team to succeed
One who has nothing to gain personally by being a leader

questions.question: What is the core meaning of Tapas, as described in the book?
options: The practice of outsourcing all of one's activities to others
A mechanism to achieve a materialistic goal, like making money
Concentrated and continuous effort directed toward a single, focused goal
A state of inaction and mental rest

questions.question: What is the physical effect of a Yajña on the offering?
options: The offering is preserved in a new form
The offering becomes a new object of worship
The offering is distributed to the attendees
The offering is completely annihilated and becomes ashes (bhasma)

questions.question: Developing a sense of detachment over time is the symbolic effect of Yajña
options: TRUE
FALSE

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the practice of Yoga Yajña?
options: A form of external sacrifice where wealth and material possessions are offered
A higher-level sacrifice focused on the practice of self-control and austerity
The eight-step path as outlined in Patañjali's Yoga Sūtra-s
The symbolic beginning of a spiritual journey

questions.question: What is identified as an 'important ingredient that one must possess to obtain knowledge'?
options: Worship
Bhakti
Bliss
Śraddhā

questions.question: What is the name for the process, practice, or methodology used to make the mind subtle?
options: Āsana
Prāņāyāma
Dhyāna
Pratyāhāra

questions.question: As per Kṛṣṇa's answer in the Gīta, what is responsible for an individual's actions and their results?
options: God is responsible for the agency, action, and results
External factors like the environment
One's own Sva-bhāva (nature)
The intentions behind the act

questions.question: According to Kṛṣṇa what two important tools are needed to fix the problem of 'mindset inertia'?
options: Focus and discipline
Practice and Dispassion
Concentration and meditation
Practice and patience

questions.question: What is the key principle that Kṛṣṇa emphasises regarding a yogī-s lifestyle?
options: Adhering to a very strict and ascetic lifestyle while minimising attention to mundane activities like sleep and food
Leading a life of extreme and unnatural conditions to enhance one's dedication
Finding a balance and moderation in one's daily behavior, such as eating and sleeping
Focusing exclusively on meditation without any attention to the external world

questions.question: What quality does the author attribute to a person who is a true yogī?
options: They perform actions with full-focus so that nothing goes wrong, and the work is guaranteed to succeed
They perform actions as required without worrying about the results (karma-phala).
They have mastered both physical postures (āsana-s) and mental focus (meditation)
They avoid material pursuits and focus only on their spiritual growth
